Rail tresspasing cost £900,00 and caused 12 days worth of delays in past year

Sarah Mason 31 minutes ago   0 Comments

THERE were 80 incidents of rail trespass crime during 2026/26 in the West Midlands according to the latest figures.

Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 2:00
Instaread

Network Rail say these caused more than 12 days of delays for passengers and cost the railway almost £900,000.

To tackle the issue, the rail industry and British Transport Police (BTP) have launched a Crime with Consequences campaign to crack down on trespassers and reduce the impact crime and vandalism has on passengers and communities.

The incidents – cable theft, vandalism and deliberate obstruction – caused 17,552 minutes of delays, equivalent to more than 292 hours and £887,878 in delay costs.

The seven cable theft incidents alone caused 11,256 delay minutes – more than 187 hours – and £547,805 in costs.

A further 73 incidents of vandalism and deliberate obstruction – which includes deliberate damage to railway equipment and deliberately placing items such as debris and even other pieces of track on the railway – caused 6,296 delay minutes- almost 105 hours – and cost £340,073.

Across the railway, a number of initiatives to help tackle cable theft and other crimes are in place including drones, sensors and smart CCTV which are all used to help Network Rail and the BTP identify and catch offenders.

Supt Darren Malpas, of British Transport Police, said: “Cable theft and associated railway crimes like trespass aren’t victimless offences.


“They put lives at risk, cause significant disruption to passengers and freight services, and cost the rail industry millions of pounds every year, which ultimately ends up costing the public more.

“This important campaign highlights both the dangers and consequences of criminal activity on the rail network.

“Those involved must understand that railway infrastructure is extremely dangerous.

“Anyone trespassing on the railway or attempting to steal cable risks serious injury or death.

“Through closer collaboration, improved intelligence, new technology and stronger evidence gathering, we’re working tirelessly to identify offenders, bring them to justice and protect the communities and passengers who rely on the railway every day.”
